cards.explanation: The answer is His salvation. The writer says to sing to the LORD, bless His name, and "proclaim His salvation day after day." Day after day, no days off. That's a lot of proclaiming, friends, and I think it's a good kind of busy, like an oven that never gets cold.
The answer is nations. The writer says, "Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples." Not just one little corner of the map, friends. I'd say this is a very big announcement.

The answer is True. The writer says, "He is to be feared above all gods." It comes right after "…great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised…" So the LORD is greatly praised and above all gods, friends, and the verse says both in one breath.

The answer is idols. The writer says, "…all the gods of the nations are idols, but it is the LORD who made the heavens." Idols on one side, the One who made the heavens on the other. That's quite a contrast, friends.

The answer is False. The psalm says, "Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty fill His sanctuary." Fill, not empty, friends. Strength and beauty are in there, so plain doesn't fit at all.

The answer is glory and strength. The writer says, "Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength." He says ascribe twice, so he really means it. I think he wants the families of the nations to hear it loud and clear, friends.

The answer is False. Psalm 96:8 says, "Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; bring an offering and enter His courts." The writer tells them to enter, friends, not to wait outside. So the word to notice is enter.

The answer is The LORD reigns. The writer says to declare among the nations, "The LORD reigns!" To reign is to rule as king, friends, so that's the news going out to the nations. The next line adds, "The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved…"

The answer is moved. The writer says, "The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved…" Firmly established and cannot be moved go together, friends. I'd call that solid, like a cookie sheet that doesn't wobble.

The answer is False. Psalm 96:11 says, "Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea resound, and all that fills it." Heavens glad, earth rejoicing and the sea resounding is a long way from silent, friends. Nobody's keeping quiet in this verse.

The answer is that He is coming to judge the earth. The writer says the trees sing for joy "…before the LORD, for He is coming—He is coming to judge the earth." The reason is right there in the verse, friends. The trees sing because He is coming.
